sourceFacts: PAH catalyses conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine.
Reduced PAH activity impairs this conversion and allows phenylalanine to accumulate.

prompt:
Create a polished original medical teaching illustration in landscape 3:2 format. Use the attached MD3 original solely as a style reference: warm watercolour/gouache on an ivory paper background, delicate ink contours, calm navy labels, muted ochre/peach/teal colours, generous whitespace and clear flat anatomical shapes. Anatomical clarity before decoration. Never photorealistic skin, glossy blood, wet flesh, fat lobules, scary faces, chunky 3D tissue blocks, or a fake scan. Only exact requested labels, clean legible short text. Footer 'Educational schematic'. No watermark, logos or attribution in the pixels. Compose an entirely new subject from the clinical specification, not the scalp content in the reference.

Two horizontal pathways, very clear hand-painted biochemistry diagram. Title 'Phenylalanine → tyrosine'. Upper heading 'Usual conversion': large teal rounded box 'Phenylalanine' on LEFT and ochre box 'Tyrosine' on RIGHT connected by a broad arrow pointing RIGHT, label ABOVE arrow 'Phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH)'. Lower heading 'PAH deficiency': same phenylalanine box with three small circles collecting underneath, same tyrosine box slightly faded; connecting rightward arrow has a small perpendicular bar interrupting it, label 'Reduced conversion'. Small bottom text 'Phenylalanine accumulates'. No molecular structures, no treatment doses, no implication of complete enzyme absence in every phenotype.
